why.why: It relies on counter-intuitive reverse psychology storytelling that creates an irresistible intrigue gap right in the first sentence.

hook_patterns: Presenting a common, embarrassing personal trait and immediately offering a psychological reason for it.
Setting up an absurd high-stakes social conflict and pausing right before the resolution.
Using counter-intuitive historical or behavioral anecdotes that defy basic logic.
todays_angle: Focus on everyday micro-behaviors that make people feel weird or insecure, framed as funny psychological superpowers between Leo and Mia.
ideas: Mia records Leo talking and plays it back to explain bone conduction psychology, triggering Leo's existential crisis over his 'real voice.'
Leo tries using the 'Potato Guarding' reverse-psychology trick to stop Mia from eating his fries, which backfires hilariously.
Mia uses psychological mirroring techniques on a pushy barista, while Leo narrates her subtle body language like an over-the-top documentary.
avoid: Generic stick-figure street fight or self-defense scenarios that lack a clear psychological twist.
Overly long historical backstories that lose the core comedy dynamic between Leo and Mia.
